newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US Dec industrial output up 0.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US Dec industrial output up 0.8 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from economists after the Federal Reserve reported that industrial production rose 0.8 percent in December and capacity utilization registered 83.8 percent.
U.S. economists in a Reuters survey expected a 0.6 percent gain in industrial production and an 83.5 percent cap use reading.
JOHN LONSKI, CHIEF ECONOMIST, MOODY'S INVESTORS SERVICE: "I think what it means is that the U.S. economy, in particular manufacturing, finished 1996 with a good deal of strength."
"What we may want to focus on would be that robust 4.1 percent annualized increase by industrial output comparing the fourth quarter to the third quarter.
"Now we have every indication that in the final three months of 1996 U.S. real GDP grew by at least 3.5 percent annualized if not 4.0 percent."

JOHN WILLIAMS, CHIEF GLOBAL MARKETS ECONOMIST, BANKERS TRUST CO: "These are very strong industrial production numbers. The industrial manufacturing component in particular was very strong. The overall number would have been even bigger if not for the fact that utility output was down sharply becuase of unseasonably warm weather. This suggests that the manufacturing sector is doing well and that there is growing momentum in the U.S. economy. This leads us to believe that the Federal Reserve will tighten this spring."
ALLEN SINAI, CHIEF GLOBAL ECONOMIST, PRIMARK DESCISION ECONOMICS: "This is a hot eocnomy, it is cooking. The production side is responding to strong sales in the fourth quarter.
"This is not just a one-quarter pickup. It is too broad based. The economy needs to replenish inventories, earnings are fueling strong income growth, which will keep supporting consumer spending.
Sinai said the 83.8 percent cap use level should capture the Federal Reserve's attention. "In the first quarter, the odds are high the Fed will raise rates at some point."

PETER D'ANTONIO, SENIOR ECONOMIST, CITICORP GLOBAL FINANCE N.A.: "The December industrial production rise was another strong number. This really pushes it up for the quarter and is one of the reasons that we and everyone else is looking for a strong fourth quarter -- because we have so much production in the quarter.

"The one thing that sticks out is that the capacity utilization rate jumped to 83.8 in December from (a revised 83.0) two months ago in October. The level, itself, is still not troublesome. But the direction and the speed at which we jumped up is troublesome."
